nodes.label: Deploy (pulumi up) job
nodes.rationale: Runs only on push to main (reviewed/merged commits, no PR credentials); job-level permissions grant id-token: write only here so no other job reaches the deployer identity; concurrency group serialises applies (cancel-in-progress: false, since a cancelled apply leaves the stack locked/half-applied); declares environment: platform as the attachment point for an optional required reviewer; deliberately no path filter, because a silently-wrong filter would skip the deploy and still report green.

nodes.label: Workload Identity Federation (GitHub OIDC to GCP)
nodes.rationale: Exchanges the run's GitHub OIDC token for short-lived credentials for the deployer service account, scoped by attributeCondition to this repository and to refs/heads/main; no service-account key exists anywhere. Writes an external-account credential file so no setup-gcloud step is needed.

nodes.label: assert-no-platform-deletes.py preflight guard
nodes.rationale: Parses the real `pulumi preview --json` plan for the exact run and aborts before `pulumi up` if it would destroy the database, media bucket, image repository, or the CI identity itself. Runs --self-test and --verify-coverage first in both the typecheck and deploy jobs, because a matcher that quietly stopped matching would pass everything, and a resource renamed in the Pulumi program while the PROTECTED list keeps the old name would still preview, apply, and report green while guarding nothing.

nodes.label: Decision: CI owns platform stack applies (Rob, 2026-08-05)
nodes.rationale: Reverses a prior 'humans only apply this stack' stance. The blast-radius argument (one shared Cloud SQL instance and media bucket, cross-tenant impact) was never an argument for humans over CI -- a human running `pulumi up` from a laptop is judged the less controlled path (ambient owner-level credential, no audit trail beyond shell history, nothing stopping an apply of uncommitted local edits). What it actually demanded was guardrails: branch restriction, short-lived scoped WIF credentials, minimal deployer grants, a delete-preflight, and an optional required-reviewer environment. Matches the pattern website/infra has run in production since 2026-08-01.
